name: Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail
_note: M2 state-executive cohort (Phase 2). Menteri Besar of Pahang since 2018 (second term from 28 Nov 2022). Added as a BN-aligned executive to balance the class. Provisional Layer B anchors pending the blind panel (minCodersToScore=3). Citations search-corroborated; reconfirm against primary sources. A5 none-on-record: the bauxite and durian-encroachment MACC matters in Pahang target other individuals, not the MB. 3R: B5 left unscored (his affidavit in the Najib house-arrest matter is contested and royalty-adjacent).

metrics.justification: No corruption charge, conviction, or MACC investigation against Wan Rosdy personally is on record; the MACC matters touching his administration (a 2024 bauxite illegal-mining bribery case, an earlier durian-encroachment probe) targeted other individuals or agency officers, and he pledged the state would fully cooperate. Recorded as the subject's own status: none on record.

citation.title: Bauxite mining corruption case: Pahang govt to fully cooperate with MACC, says Wan Rosdy

metrics.justification: In flood-prone Pahang, his administration paid RM500 special cash aid per affected household in the December 2021 monsoon floods (tens of thousands displaced) and later set aside federal flood-mitigation funds. A documented relief response in a recurrently flooded state, outcomes mixed (anchor 2).

citation.title: Floods: Victims in Pahang to get RM500 cash aid per household

metrics.justification: On 21 Nov 2023 he opened the first of a planned five permanent dedicated flood-relief centres (about RM31 million), making Pahang the first state to build relief centres solely for flood evacuees, and in May 2024 secured approval of the state's pioneer non-radioactive rare-earth project at Sungai Wang. Delivered, dated infrastructure and policy (anchor 3).

citation.title: Pahang becomes first state to build permanent relief centres solely for flood evacuees

metrics.justification: After the November 2022 state election produced a hung assembly, he assembled a cross-coalition Barisan Nasional-Pakatan Harapan government: Pahang PH submitted statutory declarations of support and the state DAP chief publicly endorsed him, with the Regent consenting to the arrangement. Documented working majority built across former rivals (anchor 3).
